title: Box shadows and text shadows
learningObjectives: Explain box shadows and text shadows and use the relevant CSS properties appropriately.

understand.concept: box-shadow draws one or more shadows around an element's box. text-shadow draws shadows behind text glyphs. Shadows can have horizontal and vertical offsets, blur, spread for box-shadow, and a colour. They do not replace adequate contrast.
understand.whyItMatters: Excessive shadows can reduce clarity and create visual clutter. Test shadows against different backgrounds and preserve readable text and visible focus indicators.
understand.analogy: A shadow suggests depth, like an object placed above a surface, but it does not change the element's layout position.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy helps visualise the effect; CSS rendering and stacking follow browser layout and painting rules.

explain.narrative: The card appears raised through a soft shadow. The shadow does not reserve additional layout space.

questions.prompt: Which property draws a shadow around an element's box?
questions.explanation: box-shadow applies shadow effects to the element's box.

questions.prompt: What should you verify when adding decorative visual effects?
options: Only whether the effect looks fashionable
Whether the effect hides focus outlines
questions.explanation: Visual effects should not make content or interactive states harder to perceive.
